brief.topic: Show users a confidence score or show them the sources?
brief.audience: PMs and designers shipping AI answers to users
constraints: Illustrative numbers labelled on screen and in caption

coreInsight: A confidence percentage asks users to trust the answer; sources and a plain 'check this' state let them verify it, so they catch more wrong answers.

hooks.text: “92% sure” doesn’t tell users what to check.
hooks.notes: Names a familiar badge and the gap in it.

hooks.text: Stop putting percentages on AI answers.
hooks.notes: Too absolute; calibrated scores can help.

hooks.text: Your confidence badge isn’t helping anyone.
hooks.notes: Vague about what to do instead.

caption.opening: A “92% confident” badge looks helpful, but it doesn’t tell users what to check, and raw model scores often aren’t well calibrated.
body:
What helps users judge an AI answer:
→ Each claim linked to the source it came from
→ A plain “check this” note when support is weak
→ A percentage only if you’ve tested that it’s calibrated
→ Checking that takes one click, not a new search
Design for verification, not just trust.
(The 1 in 5 vs 3 in 5 in the reel is illustrative, not study data.)

claims.text: Showing sources and a plain 'check this' state usually helps users judge AI answers better than an untested confidence percentage.
1 in 5 users spot a wrong answer with a score badge only vs 3 in 5 with sources and a check-this note.
